clue.text: Extra words added to uncommunicative child's complaint

parts.note: to keep mum is to stay silent, so mum means saying nothing
a PS (postscript) is extra words added at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: A child who won't talk grumbles, with a few extra words tacked on.
explanation.walkthrough: MUM here is the adjective 'silent' (as in 'keep mum'), not a mother.
explanation.definitionFit: This contagious illness, with swollen glands in the neck, is mostly caught in childhood.

clue.text: Evidence of match fixing crime: Ealing care

indicators.note: fixing suggests something tampered with, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Evidence of a match-fixing crime is found in a care home in Ealing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'match' is a wedding, not a sports fixture. Ealing is a district of west London.
explanation.definitionFit: A wedding is a union of a couple, and this official permit is the paperwork that allows it.

clue.text: Cursed heavy metal producer is pathetic; I am uplifted

indicators.note: in a down clue uplifted means the letters run upwards, so they are read in reverse

parts.note: pathetic means sad, pitiful
I'm is the short form of I am

explanation.surface: A heavy metal producer under a curse says it's pathetic, but feels better.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heavy metal' looks like rock music; it is gold, which the cursed king turned everything into. 'uplifted' turns SAD + IM into MIDAS.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek myth's king wished that everything he touched would turn to gold, and found the gift a curse.

clue.text: Member usually on the Right used to fight with Steel

definitions.text: Member usually on the Right used to fight with Steel

parts.words: Member usually on the Right used to fight with Steel
parts.note: reads like a right-wing politician fighting a man called Steel, but means the limb, usually the right one, that wields a blade

explanation.walkthrough: 'Member' suggests an MP, and 'Steel' looks like David Steel, the Liberal leader; here a member is a limb and steel is a blade.
explanation.definitionFit: Most fencers and soldiers hold the blade in the right hand, so that limb is the fighting one.

clue.text: Crack in short valley is to be steep

indicators.note: in tells us one piece is put inside the other
short means the word for valley loses its final letter

parts.note: a coombe is a short valley or hollow, especially in southern England
to have a crack at something is to have a stab at it

explanation.surface: A geologist notes a fissure in a small valley that slopes sharply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' cuts COOMBE to COOMB, and 'in' puts STAB inside it. 'Steep' means overpriced, not sloping.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang, to cost a bomb is to be very expensive, and a steep price is a high one.

clue.text: Something between shorts and shoe leather

explanation.surface: Something sits between a pair of shorts and a leather shoe.
explanation.definitionFit: The fleshy back of the lower leg shows between shorts and shoe, and young cattle hide makes fine leather.

clue.text: Pen allowed to go outside English woman's template for document

parts.note: a sty is a pen for pigs

indicators.note: to go outside means the word for allowed wraps round the next pieces

parts.note: let means allowed
she is the pronoun for a woman

explanation.surface: A pen is allowed outside, where an Englishwoman keeps a template for her document.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pen' looks like a writing tool next to 'document'; it is an animal enclosure.
explanation.definitionFit: In computing, this file sets a document's fonts and layout, acting as its design pattern.

clue.text: First man, then god's overthrown naval force

indicators.note: overthrown means turned upside down, so in a down clue the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: Adam is the first man in the Bible
Ra is the sun god of ancient Egypt

explanation.surface: First a man, then a god is overthrown by a fleet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overthrown' turns ADAM + RA upside down, giving ARMADA.
explanation.definitionFit: A fleet of warships, most famously the Spanish one sent against England in 1588.

clue.text: Courteous dances not to do in house?

indicators.note: dances suggests letters moving about, so courteous is rearranged

explanation.surface: Polite dancers decline to perform at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in house' means within the firm's own staff.
explanation.definitionFit: Firms contract work out to other companies instead of having their own staff do it.

clue.text: Violent, misspeaking don would make dull noise with gaffe

indicators.note: the don is Reverend Spooner of Oxford, famous for swapping the starting sounds of words

parts.note: a thud is a dull heavy sound
a blunder is a gaffe

explanation.surface: A violent academic, misspeaking, makes a dull noise with his blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' gives the AND that joins the two words. Swapping the first sounds of 'thud and blunder' gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes sensational melodrama full of fighting and violence, as in old adventure stories.

clue.text: Work set after radical one in which actors have no costumes

definitions.text: in which actors have no costumes

parts.note: rad is a short form of radical, as in a political radical
I is the Roman numeral for one
op, short for opus, is a work of music
to lay a table is to set it

explanation.surface: A piece of work follows a radical who performs without any costume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' tells us OP and LAY follow RAD and I. 'one' supplies I and also reads into the definition, a drama 'in which actors have no costumes'.
explanation.definitionFit: A drama broadcast for listeners needs no costumes, since no audience ever sees the cast.

clue.text: Urban trains for which Rome trolleybus provides cover

indicators.note: the words Rome trolleybus cover the answer, which sits inside them across the gap

explanation.surface: Rome's trolleybuses run over the city's underground railway.
explanation.definitionFit: A city's underground railway is called by this name in Paris and many other places.

clue.text: Indie's new location for content

indicators.note: new tells us the letters of Indie's are made into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: An independent record label moves to fresh premises.
explanation.walkthrough: Here the 's of Indie's is a real letter in the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Contents are kept within a container, so the interior is where they are found.

clue.text: It'll stuff you up, man, to speak further about Colonel

parts.note: he is the pronoun for a man

indicators.note: about means the word for speaking further goes round the abbreviation for Colonel

parts.note: to add is to say more, as in 'he added'
Col is the standard abbreviation for the army rank of Colonel

explanation.surface: Someone tells a man to go on talking about an army colonel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'man' is not a verb here; it gives HE.
explanation.definitionFit: A common viral infection blocks the nose with mucus, leaving it stuffed up.

clue.text: Rough-coated western woman, one hoisted and hung out to dry

indicators.note: in a down clue hoisted means lifted upwards, so these letters are read in reverse

parts.note: her is a pronoun for a woman
I is the Roman numeral for one
washing hung out to dry is aired

explanation.surface: A western woman in a rough coat hoists her washing and hangs it out to dry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hoisted' turns HER + I into IREH.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog breed with a coarse, wiry coat, like some terriers, is described as rough-coated.

clue.text: Give up vice, with fixed price for spirits being announced?

indicators.note: being announced means we hear the words spoken, not read them

parts.note: a ghost rate would be a set tariff for spirits, if ghosts paid for things

explanation.surface: A drinker gives up vice once a fixed price for spirits is announced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spirits' looks like alcohol but means ghosts. Said aloud, 'ghost rate' sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A reformed criminal leads an honest life from then on, giving up crime and wrongdoing.

clue.text: Length in lens mass adjusted for microscopic quality

indicators.note: in means one letter goes inside the rearranged letters
adjusted means the letters of lens and mass are rearranged

explanation.surface: A scientist adjusts the length and mass of a lens for a microscope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adjusted' rearranges LENS MASS to give SMALNESS, and 'in' puts the L of 'Length' inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Something microscopic is tiny, and tininess is the quality being described.

clue.text: Not yielding? Me neither, contrarily

indicators.note: contrarily means the phrase goes the opposite way, read from back to front

parts.note: 'nor I' is a formal way of saying 'me neither'

explanation.surface: One person refuses to give way, and another says they won't either.
explanation.definitionFit: Iron is the classic image of something hard and unbending, as in an iron will.

clue.text: Low points after crowning ascending King Edward etc.

indicators.note: after means the low points come after the other piece
in a down clue ascending means the letters run upwards, read in reverse

parts.note: atop means on top of, crowning
toes are the lowest points of the body

explanation.surface: A king is crowned, then slides to his lowest points.
explanation.walkthrough: King Edward is a popular British potato variety, not a monarch. 'ascending' turns ATOP into POTA.
explanation.definitionFit: This well-known British variety is a floury spud, so it stands for its whole kind.

clue.text: Common sense having left clot

parts.note: a clot is British slang for a stupid person, an oaf

explanation.surface: Common sense has deserted some idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Use your loaf' is British rhyming slang (loaf of bread = head) for 'use your common sense'.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang your head stands for good sense, so using it means thinking sensibly.

clue.text: Charitable inclination to keep backing Darling

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Charitable inclination to keep backing Darling': BENT (inclination) around EVOL (LOVE, darling, reversed) gives BENEVOLT; the EN the answer needs comes from no word, so a word looks missing and no source gives the full clue.
annotationWithheld.clue: Charitable inclination to keep backing Darling

clue.text: Raise makes another bob for the rest

indicators.note: in a down clue raise means lift upwards, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: to bob is to dip, so bobbing again redips

explanation.surface: A raise earns another shilling for everyone else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bob' looks like an old shilling coin; it is a dip. In snooker, a spider is a cue rest with a tall arch.
explanation.definitionFit: In snooker, players use this long arched cue support to reach a ball beyond other balls.

clue.text: Alternative group of 12 crossed with 9?

indicators.note: crossed with means two parents are bred together, so the result takes one part from each

parts.note: the second word of the answer to 12 across
the second word of the answer to 9 across

explanation.surface: A band is bred from two other grid answers, like a hybrid plant.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'crossing' of 12 and 9 takes the second word of each. Its twin at 26 across takes the first words. 'Alternative' means alternative rock, a style of music.
explanation.definitionFit: A British rock band formed in London in the 1990s, usually filed under alternative rock.

clue.text: Wonderful place anxiety reliever found with 25 regular doses of drug

indicators.note: the answer to 25 across means without a finish, so the drug's name loses its last letter

parts.note: Xanax is a brand of drug prescribed for anxiety

indicators.note: regular doses means taking every other letter of drug

explanation.surface: An anxiety drug works with regular doses of another drug to create a wonderful place.
explanation.walkthrough: From 'drug' the alternate letters are D and U.
explanation.definitionFit: Coleridge's poem describes a dreamlike pleasure palace, and the name now stands for any idyllic place.

clue.text: Ward off limits for vaccine, contained by design

indicators.note: contained by means the first and last letters of vaccine go inside the word for design

parts.note: art can mean design, as in graphic art

indicators.note: the limits of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A vaccine's limits are shaped by its design to fight off disease.
explanation.walkthrough: The first and last letters of 'vaccine' are V and E; ART goes round them.
explanation.definitionFit: To prevent or turn aside a danger before it can strike is to stop it coming.

clue.text: Old German word for the river bordering Poland

parts.note: der is a German word for 'the'

explanation.surface: An old German word names the river on Poland's border.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the' is part of the wordplay, not the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: This river runs along much of the frontier between Germany and its eastern neighbour.

clue.text: Last of bottled gas used for lighting back lots

indicators.note: back means the whole run of letters is read backwards
last of means only the final letter of the word bottled is taken

parts.note: neon is the gas that glows in illuminated signs

explanation.surface: Gas left at the bottom of a bottle is used to light the back lots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns D + NEON into NOEN + D.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'no end of' means a great amount, so it works as a casual word for plenty.

clue.text: Alternative group of 9 crossed with 12?

indicators.note: crossed with means two parents are bred together, so the result takes one part from each

parts.note: the first word of the answer to 9 across
the first word of the answer to 12 across

explanation.surface: A band is bred from two other grid answers, like a hybrid plant.
explanation.walkthrough: This time the crossing takes the first word of each entry. Its twin at 21 across takes the second words. 'Alternative' means alternative rock.
explanation.definitionFit: An English rock band from Oxfordshire, a leading name in alternative rock.

clue.text: Film contract's undemanding stipulation?

explanation.surface: A film contract includes a clause that asks very little.
explanation.walkthrough: A rider is a clause added to a contract, so an undemanding one is easy.
explanation.definitionFit: A 1969 road movie starring Dennis Hopper and Peter Fonda, and also a lenient extra clause in a deal.

clue.text: Tried to pass younger, oversexed man

parts.note: to sit an exam is to try to pass it
yr is a standard abbreviation for younger

explanation.surface: A younger man tried to get by on his sex appeal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tried to pass' sounds like an exam: SAT, as in sat a test.
explanation.definitionFit: A woodland creature of Greek myth known for its lust, so the word now means a lecherous man.
